find: REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION updater_health_counts() FROM PUBLIC;
replace: -- mutation: PUBLIC keeps the default EXECUTE
test: pnpm db:ledger && PG_BIN="${PG_BIN:-/opt/homebrew/opt/postgresql@17/bin}" CONTROL_ROOM_PG_TEST_PORT_BASE="${CONTROL_ROOM_PG_TEST_PORT_BASE:-59870}" node scripts/run-tests-with-quarantine.mjs --import tsx --test --test-concurrency=1 --test-timeout=600000 tests/updater-health-counts-direct.test.ts; git checkout -- deploy/postgres/migration-ledger.json
why: PostgreSQL grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC on every new function, so without this REVOKE any login on the socket could ask the definer for the counts (R20d: counts only, to the updater)

test: pnpm db:ledger && PG_BIN="${PG_BIN:-/opt/homebrew/opt/postgresql@17/bin}" CONTROL_ROOM_PG_TEST_PORT_BASE="${CONTROL_ROOM_PG_TEST_PORT_BASE:-59870}" node scripts/run-tests-with-quarantine.mjs --import tsx --test --test-concurrency=1 --test-timeout=600000 tests/updater-health-counts-direct.test.ts; git checkout -- deploy/postgres/migration-ledger.json
why: an EXECUTE grantee the design does not name must be refused at apply time, not discovered later

find: AND p.prosecdef AND p.provolatile = 's' AND p.prokind = 'f' AND p.pronargs = 0
test: pnpm db:ledger && PG_BIN="${PG_BIN:-/opt/homebrew/opt/postgresql@17/bin}" CONTROL_ROOM_PG_TEST_PORT_BASE="${CONTROL_ROOM_PG_TEST_PORT_BASE:-59870}" node scripts/run-tests-with-quarantine.mjs --import tsx --test --test-concurrency=1 --test-timeout=600000 tests/updater-health-counts-direct.test.ts; git checkout -- deploy/postgres/migration-ledger.json
why: the boundary must stay SECURITY DEFINER, STABLE and zero-argument; a VOLATILE or arg-taking function would be a proxy for an arbitrary SELECT through the definer

find:
AND p.proconfig = ARRAY['search_path=pg_catalog, public, pg_temp']::text[])
    THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'updater health count function must be STABLE SECURITY DEFINER
test: pnpm db:ledger && PG_BIN="${PG_BIN:-/opt/homebrew/opt/postgresql@17/bin}" CONTROL_ROOM_PG_TEST_PORT_BASE="${CONTROL_ROOM_PG_TEST_PORT_BASE:-59870}" node scripts/run-tests-with-quarantine.mjs --import tsx --test --test-concurrency=1 --test-timeout=600000 tests/updater-health-counts-direct.test.ts; git checkout -- deploy/postgres/migration-ledger.json
why: the pinned search_path is what stops candidate SQL shadowing an object the definer's body names (R10b); dropping it must be caught

find:
WHERE p.oid = fn AND a.privilege_type = 'EXECUTE' AND a.is_grantable
        AND pg_catalog.pg_get_userbyid(a.grantee) = 'control_room_deployer') THEN
replace:
WHERE p.oid = fn AND a.privilege_type = 'EXECUTE' AND false
        AND pg_catalog.pg_get_userbyid(a.grantee) = 'control_room_deployer') THEN
test: pnpm db:ledger && PG_BIN="${PG_BIN:-/opt/homebrew/opt/postgresql@17/bin}" CONTROL_ROOM_PG_TEST_PORT_BASE="${CONTROL_ROOM_PG_TEST_PORT_BASE:-59870}" node scripts/run-tests-with-quarantine.mjs --import tsx --test --test-concurrency=1 --test-timeout=600000 tests/updater-health-counts-direct.test.ts; git checkout -- deploy/postgres/migration-ledger.json
why: a GRANTABLE EXECUTE would let the updater's login hand this definer's reach to anybody, which is the exact authority growth the function exists not to permit

test: pnpm db:ledger && PG_BIN="${PG_BIN:-/opt/homebrew/opt/postgresql@17/bin}" CONTROL_ROOM_PG_TEST_PORT_BASE="${CONTROL_ROOM_PG_TEST_PORT_BASE:-59870}" node scripts/run-tests-with-quarantine.mjs --import tsx --test --test-concurrency=1 --test-timeout=600000 tests/updater-health-counts-direct.test.ts; git checkout -- deploy/postgres/migration-ledger.json
why: workspaces has no unique constraint on tenant_id alone, so an ambiguous scope would silently DOUBLE every count -- and a health signal that doubles still says healthy

find: EXECUTE 'GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.updater_health_counts() TO control_room_deployer';
replace: -- mutation: the updater's login is never granted the health counts
why: without this grant the updater's independent read cannot run at all and §8.4's count comparison can never be satisfied

find: REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION updater_health_counts() FROM control_room_deployer;
replace: -- mutation: the down migration leaves the grant behind
why: a down migration that dropped the function but left a grant behind is not a reversal; it is an upgrade that cannot be rolled back the way it went up
a count arriving from the database must be digits only; accepting any string would let a malformed driver value through the comparison against the signed web response
the authority read must return exactly the three counts and nothing else; extra columns from a future migration must refuse here rather than flow into the health response
zero rows means an unbound or ambiguous scope and must fail closed; more than one means this is not the database the adapter was bound to
§8.4 requires the web login's INSERT on updater.plan_approvals; a false result is the whole signal that the approval path is broken, so it must refuse health rather than report it
an error page renders perfectly happily; counting its bytes as a healthy Home would make a broken server look healthy
§8.4 requires a NON-EMPTY render; an empty body must refuse, and an implausibly large one must not be reported as a healthy page
